evidence: A calculation on published values: present-day temperature profiles (Kuskov & Kronrod 2009, Karato 2013, Khan et al. 2014, digitised), Hirth & Kohlstedt's (2003) olivine flow laws with stated grain size, water and stress, the crustal-loading study's interior (Briaud et al. 2023) and low-viscosity zone (Harada et al. 2014). Love numbers of a self-gravitating, incompressible Maxwell Moon by the correspondence principle at real s and a fitted relaxation spectrum, checked against closed forms, the crustal-loading study's elastic numbers, elastic lids over a fluid interior and the monthly tide. Not validated against any observed loading of the present Moon; the flow laws are measured on Earth's olivine.
reading_rule: Read 'central' as the response of the present Moon's mid-range thermal state and 'soft' and 'stiff' as its bounds; series are the response to a load applied at t = 0 (years). k'_n(t) multiplies a load's own potential; the Moon-wide inertia of a load is (1 + k'_2(t)) times its rigid inertia. The tidal k_2(t) is the bulge's re-formation per unit forcing. Spectra hold elastic + sum a_j (1 - exp(-r_j t)) on rates_per_year. The full degree 2-50 tables are on the research drive.

study_m.about: Floors where the seas are deeper than 2 km (2.8 km on average) against the mean land, held at 28%: elastic 17 m, relaxed 370-620 m over Te 75-20 km (490 m at 40 km), 240 m at 150 km
